e-4936.knowledge_point: Finding the Cartesian Equation of the Plane Perpendicular To a Given Vector
e-4936.problem: Find a Cartesian equation of the plane that passes through the point $P(9,-2,3)$ and is perpendicular to the vector $\mathbf{n}=3\mathbf{i}-4\mathbf{j}+7\mathbf{k}.$
e-4936.worked_solution:
First, we note that the position vector of the point $P$ is $\mathbf{p}=\langle 9,-2,3 \rangle$ and the normal vector of the plane is $\mathbf{n}=\langle 3,-4,7 \rangle.$

Using the dot product, we can find the equation of the plane as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}(r-p)\cdot n & =0 \\ r\cdot n & =p\cdot n \\ r\cdot ⟨3,-4,7⟩ & =⟨9,-2,3⟩\cdot ⟨3,-4,7⟩ \\ r\cdot ⟨3,-4,7⟩ & =56.\end{aligned}
$$

Now, to obtain the Cartesian equation of the plane, we substitute $\mathbf{r}=\langle x,y,z \rangle$ into the equation above and get

$$
\begin{aligned}⟨x,y,z⟩\cdot ⟨3,-4,7⟩ & =56 \\ 3x-4y+7z & =56 \\ 3x-4y+7z-56 & =0.\end{aligned}
$$

e-4937.knowledge_point: Finding the Cartesian Equation of the Plane Perpendicular To a Given Line
e-4937.problem:
Find a Cartesian equation of the plane that passes through the point $P(-1,4,8)$ and is perpendicular to the line 
$\dfrac{x+3}{-5}=\dfrac{y-1}{3}=\dfrac{z+2}{2}.$
e-4937.worked_solution:
First, we note that the position vector of $P$ is $\mathbf{p}=\langle -1,4,8 \rangle.$ From the canonical equation, we find that the line is parallel to the vector $\langle -5,3,2 \rangle.$ So, the normal vector of the plane is 

$$
\mathbf{n}=\langle -5,3,2 \rangle.
$$

Using the dot product, we can find the equation of the plane as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}(r-p)\cdot n & =0 \\ r\cdot n & =p\cdot n \\ r\cdot ⟨-5,3,2⟩ & =⟨-1,4,8⟩\cdot ⟨-5,3,2⟩ \\ r\cdot ⟨-5,3,2⟩ & =33\end{aligned}
$$

Now, to obtain the Cartesian equation of the plane, we substitute $\mathbf{r}=\langle x,y,z \rangle$ into the equation above and get

$$
\begin{aligned}⟨x,y,z⟩\cdot ⟨-5,3,2⟩ & =33 \\ -5x+3y+2z & =33 \\ -5x+3y+2z-33 & =0.\end{aligned}
$$

e-4938.knowledge_point: Finding the Vector Equation of a Plane Given Its Cartesian Equation
e-4938.problem: Given the Cartesian equation $2x-y+z+13=0$ of the plane $\Pi,$ find an equation of $\Pi$ in the form $(\mathbf{r}-\mathbf{p})\cdot\mathbf{n}=0.$
e-4938.worked_solution:
First, from the coefficients in equation of the plane, we get that the normal vector of $\Pi$ is $\mathbf{n}=\langle 2,-1,1 \rangle.$

Now, we solve the Cartesian equation of $\Pi$ for $z\mathbin{:}$

$$
\begin{aligned}2x-y+z+13 & =0 \\ z & =-2x+y-13\end{aligned}
$$

If we put, say, $x=0$ and $y=0,$ we get $z=-13.$ So, the point $P(0,0,-13)$ lies on $\Pi.$ Note that the position vector of $P$ is $\mathbf{p}=\langle 0,0,-13 \rangle.$

Finally, we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}(r-p)\cdot n & =0 \\ (r-⟨0,0,-13⟩)\cdot ⟨2,-1,1⟩ & =0.\end{aligned}
$$

e-4939.knowledge_point: Finding the Cartesian Equation of the Plane Parallel To Two Vectors
e-4939.problem: Find a Cartesian equation of the plane that passes through the point $P(-3,2,-6)$ and is parallel to the vectors $\mathbf{v_1}=\langle -3, 5, 2 \rangle$ and $\mathbf{v_2}=\langle 1, 3, -2 \rangle.$
e-4939.worked_solution:
First, we note that the position vector of the point $P$ is $\mathbf{p}=\langle -3,2,-6 \rangle.$

Now, we need to find the normal vector of the plane. To do that, we use the cross product of $\mathbf{v_1}$ and $\mathbf{v_2}$ as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}n & ={v}_{1}\times {v}_{2} \\  & =[\begin{aligned}-3 \\ 5 \\ 2\end{aligned}]\times [\begin{aligned}1 \\ 3 \\ -2\end{aligned}] \\  & =\left|\begin{aligned}i & j & k \\ -3 & 5 & 2 \\ 1 & 3 & -2\end{aligned}\right| \\  & =-16i-4j-14k \\  & =⟨-16,-4,-14⟩\end{aligned}
$$

Then, using the dot product, we can find the equation of the plane:

$$
\begin{aligned}(r-p)\cdot n & =0 \\ r\cdot n & =p\cdot n \\ r\cdot ⟨-16,-4,-14⟩ & =⟨-3,2,-6⟩\cdot ⟨-16,-4,-14⟩ \\ r\cdot ⟨-16,-4,-14⟩ & =124\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, to obtain the Cartesian equation of the plane, we substitute $\mathbf{r}=\langle x,y,z \rangle$ into the equation above and get

$$
\begin{aligned}⟨x,y,z⟩\cdot ⟨-16,-4,-14⟩ & =124 \\ -16x-4y-14z & =124 \\ -16x-4y-14z-124 & =0 \\ 8x+2y+7z+62 & =0.\end{aligned}
$$

after.name: Question 1
after.problem: Find a Cartesian equation of the plane that passes through the point $P(1,-2,4)$ and is perpendicular to the vector $n=⟨0,3,-5⟩.$
after.worked_solution:
First, we note that the position vector of the point $P$ is $p=⟨1,-2,4⟩$ and the normal vector of the plane is $n=⟨0,3,-5⟩.$

Using the dot product we can find an equation of the plane as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}(r-p)\cdot n & =0 \\ r\cdot n & =p\cdot n \\ r\cdot ⟨0,3,-5⟩ & =⟨1,-2,4⟩\cdot ⟨0,3,-5⟩ \\ r\cdot ⟨0,3,-5⟩ & =-26\end{aligned}
$$

Now, to obtain the Cartesian equation of the plane, we substitute $r=⟨x,y,z⟩$ into the equation above. Hence,

$$
\begin{aligned}⟨x,y,z⟩\cdot ⟨0,3,-5⟩ & =-26 \\ 3y-5z & =-26 \\ 3y-5z+26 & =0.\end{aligned}
$$

content.problem: Find a Cartesian equation of the plane that passes through the point $P(1,-2,4)$ and is perpendicular to the vector $n=⟨0,3,-5⟩.$
content.worked_solution:
First, we note that the position vector of the point $P$ is $p=⟨1,-2,4⟩$ and the normal vector of the plane is $n=⟨0,3,-5⟩.$

Using the dot product we can find an equation of the plane as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}(r-p)\cdot n & =0 \\ r\cdot n & =p\cdot n \\ r\cdot ⟨0,3,-5⟩ & =⟨1,-2,4⟩\cdot ⟨0,3,-5⟩ \\ r\cdot ⟨0,3,-5⟩ & =-26\end{aligned}
$$

Now, to obtain the Cartesian equation of the plane, we substitute $r=⟨x,y,z⟩$ into the equation above. Hence,

$$
\begin{aligned}⟨x,y,z⟩\cdot ⟨0,3,-5⟩ & =-26 \\ 3y-5z & =-26 \\ 3y-5z+26 & =0.\end{aligned}
$$

after.worked_solution:

Using the dot product, we can find the equation of the plane as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}(r-p)\cdot n & =0 \\ r\cdot n & =p\cdot n \\ r\cdot ⟨3,-1,2⟩ & =⟨5,2,-1⟩\cdot ⟨3,-1,2⟩ \\ r\cdot ⟨3,-1,2⟩ & =11.\end{aligned}

$$
\begin{aligned}⟨x,y,z⟩\cdot ⟨3,-1,2⟩ & =11 \\ 3x-y+2z & =11 \\ 3x-y+2z-11 & =0.\end{aligned}
$$

Question 3
?

Find a Cartesian equation of the plane that passes through the point P(−2,1,−3) and is perpendicular to the vector n=⟨−2,7,−1⟩.

a
7x−2y−z+19=0
b
−2x+7y−z−14=0
c
−2x+7y+z−11=0
d
−x+7y−2z+15=0
e
−x+2y−7z−7=0
Submit
Incorrect
EXPLANATION

First, we note that the position vector of the point P is p=⟨−2,1,−3⟩ and the normal vector of the plane is n=⟨−2,7,−1⟩.

Using the dot product we can find an equation of the plane as follows: (r−p)⋅n=0r⋅n=p⋅nr⋅⟨−2,7,−1⟩=⟨−2,1,−3⟩⋅⟨−2,7,−1⟩r⋅⟨−2,7,−1⟩=14.

Now, to obtain the Cartesian equation of the plane, we substitute r=⟨x,y,z⟩ into the equation above. Hence, ⟨x,y,z⟩⋅⟨−2,7,−1⟩=14−2x+7y−z=14−2x+7y−z−14=0.

verification.explanation: The revealed solution confirms option b: the normal is (-2,7,-1), and its dot product with P is 4+7+3=14. Thus the plane is -2x+7y-z-14=0. Substituting P gives zero.

content.knowledge_point: Finding the Cartesian Equation of the Plane Perpendicular To a Given Vector
content.problem: Find a Cartesian equation of the plane that passes through the point $P(-2,1,-3)$ and is perpendicular to the vector $n=⟨-2,7,-1⟩.$
content.worked_solution:
First, we note that the position vector of the point $P$ is $p=⟨-2,1,-3⟩$ and the normal vector of the plane is $n=⟨-2,7,-1⟩.$

Using the dot product we can find an equation of the plane as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}(r-p)\cdot n & =0 \\ r\cdot n & =p\cdot n \\ r\cdot ⟨-2,7,-1⟩ & =⟨-2,1,-3⟩\cdot ⟨-2,7,-1⟩ \\ r\cdot ⟨-2,7,-1⟩ & =14.\end{aligned}
$$

Now, to obtain the Cartesian equation of the plane, we substitute $r=⟨x,y,z⟩$ into the equation above. Hence,

$$
\begin{aligned}⟨x,y,z⟩\cdot ⟨-2,7,-1⟩ & =14 \\ -2x+7y-z & =14 \\ -2x+7y-z-14 & =0.\end{aligned}
$$

Question 4
?

Find a Cartesian equation of the plane that passes through the point P(−2,3,−1) and is perpendicular to the vector n=3i+4j−k.

a
3x−4y−z+9=0
b
3x+4y−z−7=0
c
4x+3y−z−11=0
d
x+3y−4z−17=0
e
4x−3y−z+13=0
Submit
Correct
EXPLANATION

First, we note that the position vector of the point P is p=⟨−2,3,−1⟩ and the normal vector of the plane is n=⟨3,4,−1⟩.

Using the dot product, we can find the equation of the plane as follows:

(r−p)⋅n=0r⋅n=p⋅nr⋅⟨3,4,−1⟩=⟨−2,3,−1⟩⋅⟨3,4,−1⟩r⋅⟨3,4,−1⟩=7.

Now, to obtain the Cartesian equation of the plane, we substitute r=⟨x,y,z⟩ into the equation above and get

⟨x,y,z⟩⋅⟨3,4,−1⟩=73x+4y−z=73x+4y−z−7=0.

content.knowledge_point: Finding the Cartesian Equation of the Plane Perpendicular To a Given Vector
content.problem: Find a Cartesian equation of the plane that passes through the point $P(-2,3,-1)$ and is perpendicular to the vector $n=3i+4j-k.$
content.worked_solution:
First, we note that the position vector of the point $P$ is $p=⟨-2,3,-1⟩$ and the normal vector of the plane is $n=⟨3,4,-1⟩.$

Using the dot product, we can find the equation of the plane as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}(r-p)\cdot n & =0 \\ r\cdot n & =p\cdot n \\ r\cdot ⟨3,4,-1⟩ & =⟨-2,3,-1⟩\cdot ⟨3,4,-1⟩ \\ r\cdot ⟨3,4,-1⟩ & =7.\end{aligned}
$$

Now, to obtain the Cartesian equation of the plane, we substitute $r=⟨x,y,z⟩$ into the equation above and get

$$
\begin{aligned}⟨x,y,z⟩\cdot ⟨3,4,-1⟩ & =7 \\ 3x+4y-z & =7 \\ 3x+4y-z-7 & =0.\end{aligned}
$$

Question 5
?

Find a Cartesian equation of the plane that passes through the point P(−4,3,0) and is perpendicular to the vector n=2i+5j−8k.

a
2x+5y−8z−7=0
b
2x+5y−8z−1=0
c
−4x+3y+z+7=0
d
−4x+3y−7=0
e
2x+5y−8z−17=0
Submit
Correct
EXPLANATION

First, we note that the position vector of the point P is p=⟨−4,3,0⟩ and the normal vector of the plane is n=⟨2,5,−8⟩.

Using the dot product we can find the equation of the plane as follows: (r−p)⋅n=0r⋅n=p⋅nr⋅⟨2,5,−8⟩=⟨−4,3,0⟩⋅⟨2,5,−8⟩r⋅⟨2,5,−8⟩=7.

Now, to obtain the Cartesian equation of the plane, we substitute r=⟨x,y,z⟩ into the equation above. Hence, ⟨x,y,z⟩⋅⟨2,5,−8⟩=72x+5y−8z=72x+5y−8z−7=0.

content.problem: Find a Cartesian equation of the plane that passes through the point $P(-4,3,0)$ and is perpendicular to the vector $n=2i+5j-8k.$
content.worked_solution:
First, we note that the position vector of the point $P$ is $p=⟨-4,3,0⟩$ and the normal vector of the plane is $n=⟨2,5,-8⟩.$

Using the dot product we can find the equation of the plane as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}(r-p)\cdot n & =0 \\ r\cdot n & =p\cdot n \\ r\cdot ⟨2,5,-8⟩ & =⟨-4,3,0⟩\cdot ⟨2,5,-8⟩ \\ r\cdot ⟨2,5,-8⟩ & =7.\end{aligned}
$$

Now, to obtain the Cartesian equation of the plane, we substitute $r=⟨x,y,z⟩$ into the equation above. Hence,

$$
\begin{aligned}⟨x,y,z⟩\cdot ⟨2,5,-8⟩ & =7 \\ 2x+5y-8z & =7 \\ 2x+5y-8z-7 & =0.\end{aligned}
$$

after.problem:

${\begin{aligned}x=-2+t \\ y=1+4t \\ z=5\end{aligned}.$
after.worked_solution:
First, we note that the position vector of $P$ is $p=⟨2,-4,1⟩.$  From the parametrical equation, we find that the line is parallel to the vector $⟨1,4,0⟩.$  So, the normal vector of the plane is 

$$
n=⟨1,4,0⟩.
$$

Using the dot product, we can find the equation of the plane as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}(r-p)\cdot n & =0 \\ r\cdot n & =p\cdot n \\ r\cdot ⟨1,4,0⟩ & =⟨2,-4,1⟩\cdot ⟨1,4,0⟩ \\ r\cdot ⟨1,4,0⟩ & =-14\end{aligned}
$$

Now, to obtain the Cartesian equation of the plane, we substitute $r=⟨x,y,z⟩$ into the equation above. Hence,

$$

content.knowledge_point: Finding the Cartesian Equation of the Plane Perpendicular To a Given Line
content.problem:
Find a Cartesian equation of the plane that passes through the point $P(2,-4,1)$ and is perpendicular to the line 
${\begin{aligned}x=-2+t \\ y=1+4t \\ z=5\end{aligned}.$
content.worked_solution:
First, we note that the position vector of $P$ is $p=⟨2,-4,1⟩.$  From the parametrical equation, we find that the line is parallel to the vector $⟨1,4,0⟩.$  So, the normal vector of the plane is 

$$
n=⟨1,4,0⟩.
$$

Using the dot product, we can find the equation of the plane as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}(r-p)\cdot n & =0 \\ r\cdot n & =p\cdot n \\ r\cdot ⟨1,4,0⟩ & =⟨2,-4,1⟩\cdot ⟨1,4,0⟩ \\ r\cdot ⟨1,4,0⟩ & =-14\end{aligned}
$$

Now, to obtain the Cartesian equation of the plane, we substitute $r=⟨x,y,z⟩$ into the equation above. Hence,

$$
\begin{aligned}⟨x,y,z⟩\cdot ⟨1,4,0⟩ & =-14 \\ x+4y & =-14 \\ x+4y+14 & =0.\end{aligned}
$$

Find a Cartesian equation of the plane that passes through the point P(2,3,−1) and is perpendicular to the line r=[−201]+t[32−2].

a
−2x+y+z−2=0
b
3x+2y−2z−14=0
c
2x−z−14=0
d
2x+3y−z−14=0
e
3x+2y−2z−2=0
Submit

decision.explanation: The line direction (3,2,-2) is normal to the plane. Through P(2,3,-1), its equation is 3(x-2)+2(y-3)-2(z+1)=0, which expands to 3x+2y-2z-14=0, option b.

after.name: Question 8
after.problem:
Find a Cartesian equation of the plane that passes through the point $P(2,3,-1)$ and is perpendicular to the line 
$r=[\begin{aligned}-2 \\ 0 \\ 1\end{aligned}]+t[\begin{aligned}3 \\ 2 \\ -2\end{aligned}].$
after.worked_solution:
First, we note that the position vector of $P$ is $p=⟨2,3,-1⟩.$ From the vectorial equation, we find that the line is parallel to the vector $⟨3,2,-2⟩.$ So, the normal vector of the plane is 

$$
n=⟨3,2,-2⟩.
$$

Using the dot product, we can find the equation of the plane as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}(r-p)\cdot n & =0 \\ r\cdot n & =p\cdot n \\ r\cdot ⟨3,2,-2⟩ & =⟨2,3,-1⟩\cdot ⟨3,2,-2⟩ \\ r\cdot ⟨3,2,-2⟩ & =14.\end{aligned}
$$

Now, to obtain the Cartesian equation of the plane, we substitute $r=⟨x,y,z⟩$ into the equation above. Hence,

$$
\begin{aligned}⟨x,y,z⟩\cdot ⟨3,2,-2⟩ & =14 \\ 3x+2y-2z & =14 \\ 3x+2y-2z-14 & =0.\end{aligned}
$$

before.problem:
Find a Cartesian equation of the plane that passes through the point $P(3,-2,1)$ and is perpendicular to the line 

$$

after.name: Question 9
after.problem:
Find a Cartesian equation of the plane that passes through the point $P(3,-2,1)$ and is perpendicular to the line 

$$
\frac{x-1}{5}=\frac{z+2}{-3},\,y=4
$$
after.worked_solution:
First, we note that the position vector of $P$ is $p=⟨3,-2,1⟩.$ From the Cartesian equation, we find that the line is parallel to the vector $⟨5,0,-3⟩.$ So, the normal vector of the plane is 

$$
n=⟨5,0,-3⟩.
$$

Using the dot product, we can find the equation of the plane as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}(r-p)\cdot n & =0 \\ r\cdot n & =p\cdot n \\ r\cdot ⟨5,0,-3⟩ & =⟨3,-2,1⟩\cdot ⟨5,0,-3⟩ \\ r\cdot ⟨5,0,-3⟩ & =12\end{aligned}
$$

Now, to obtain the Cartesian equation of the plane, we substitute $r=⟨x,y,z⟩$ into the equation above and get

$$
\begin{aligned}⟨x,y,z⟩\cdot ⟨5,0,-3⟩ & =12 \\ 5x-3z & =12 \\ 5x-3z-12 & =0.\end{aligned}
$$

n=⟨5,0,−3⟩.

decision.explanation: The line direction (-2,0,7) is normal to the plane. Through P(3,0,-2), its equation is -2(x-3)+7(z+2)=0, which expands to -2x+7z+20=0, option b.

after.name: Question 10
after.problem:
Find a Cartesian equation of the plane that passes through the point $P(3,0,-2)$ and is perpendicular to the line 
${\begin{aligned}x=7-2t \\ y=7 \\ z=7t\end{aligned}.$
after.worked_solution:
First, we note that the position vector of $P$ is $p=⟨3,0,-2⟩.$ From the parametrical equation, we find that the line is parallel to the vector $⟨-2,0,7⟩.$ So, the normal vector of the plane is 

$$
n=⟨-2,0,7⟩.
$$

Using the dot product, we can find the equation of the plane as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}(r-p)\cdot n & =0 \\ r\cdot n & =p\cdot n \\ r\cdot ⟨-2,0,7⟩ & =⟨3,0,-2⟩\cdot ⟨-2,0,7⟩ \\ r\cdot ⟨-2,0,7⟩ & =-20.\end{aligned}
$$

Now, to obtain the Cartesian equation of the plane, we substitute $r=⟨x,y,z⟩$ into the equation above. Hence,

$$
\begin{aligned}⟨x,y,z⟩\cdot ⟨-2,0,7⟩ & =-20 \\ -2x+7z & =-20 \\ -2x+7z+20 & =0.\end{aligned}
$$

a

b
−2x+7z+20=0
c
−x+7z+5=0
d
−2y+7z+10=0
e
−7x+7y+7z−20=0
Submit
Correct

First, we note that the position vector of P is p=⟨3,0,−2⟩. From the parametrical equation, we find that the line is parallel to the vector ⟨−2,0,7⟩. So, the normal vector of the plane is

n=⟨−2,0,7⟩.

Using the dot product, we can find the equation of the plane as follows:

(r−p)⋅n=0r⋅n=p⋅nr⋅⟨−2,0,7⟩=⟨3,0,−2⟩⋅⟨−2,0,7⟩r⋅⟨−2,0,7⟩=−20.

Now, to obtain the Cartesian equation of the plane, we substitute r=⟨x,y,z⟩ into the equation above. Hence, ⟨x,y,z⟩⋅⟨−2,0,7⟩=−20−2x+7z=−20−2x+7z+20=0.

before.html:
Question 11
?

Given the Cartesian equation x−y+4z+16=0 of the plane Π, find an equation of Π in the form (r−p)⋅n=0.

a
(r−⟨0,0,1⟩)⋅⟨1,−1,4⟩=0
b
(r−⟨0,0,−4⟩)⋅⟨1,−1,4⟩=0
c
(r−⟨0,0,1⟩)⋅⟨−1,−1,16⟩=0
d
(r−⟨0,0,−1⟩)⋅⟨1,0,4⟩=0
e
(r−⟨0,0,4⟩)⋅⟨1,−1,4⟩=0
Submit

decision.explanation: The coefficients give the normal vector ⟨1,-1,4⟩. Setting x=y=0 gives z=-4, so ⟨0,0,-4⟩ is a point on the plane. Option b expands to x-y+4(z+4)=0, the given equation.

after.name: Question 11
after.problem: Given the Cartesian equation $x-y+4z+16=0$ of the plane $Π$, find an equation of $Π$ in the form $(r-p)\cdot n=0.$
after.worked_solution:
First, from the equation of the plane we get that the normal vector of $Π$ is $n=⟨1,-1,4⟩.$

Now, we solve the Cartesian equation of $Π$ for $z$:

$$
\begin{aligned}x-y+4z+16 & =0 \\ z & =-\frac{1}{4}x+\frac{1}{4}y-4.\end{aligned}
$$

If we put, say, $x=0$ and $y=0$, we get $z=-4.$ Hence, the point $P(0,0,-4)$ lies on $Π.$ Note that the position vector of $P$ is $p=⟨0,0,-4⟩.$

Finally, we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}(r-p)\cdot n & =0 \\ (r-⟨0,0,-4⟩)\cdot ⟨1,-1,4⟩ & =0.\end{aligned}
$$

Question 11
?

Given the Cartesian equation x−y+4z+16=0 of the plane Π, find an equation of Π in the form (r−p)⋅n=0.

a
(r−⟨0,0,1⟩)⋅⟨1,−1,4⟩=0
b
(r−⟨0,0,−4⟩)⋅⟨1,−1,4⟩=0
c
(r−⟨0,0,1⟩)⋅⟨−1,−1,16⟩=0
d
(r−⟨0,0,−1⟩)⋅⟨1,0,4⟩=0
e
(r−⟨0,0,4⟩)⋅⟨1,−1,4⟩=0
Submit
Incorrect
EXPLANATION

First, from the equation of the plane we get that the normal vector of Π is n=⟨1,−1,4⟩.

Now, we solve the Cartesian equation of Π for z: x−y+4z+16=0z=−14x+14y−4. If we put, say, x=0 and y=0, we get z=−4. Hence, the point P(0,0,−4) lies on Π. Note that the position vector of P is p=⟨0,0,−4⟩.

Finally, we obtain (r−p)⋅n=0(r−⟨0,0,−4⟩)⋅⟨1,−1,4⟩=0.

verification.explanation: The revealed solution confirms normal ⟨1,-1,4⟩ and point (0,0,-4). Option b expands to x-y+4(z+4)=0, exactly x-y+4z+16=0.

content.knowledge_point: Finding the Vector Equation of a Plane Given Its Cartesian Equation
content.problem: Given the Cartesian equation $x-y+4z+16=0$ of the plane $Π$, find an equation of $Π$ in the form $(r-p)\cdot n=0.$
content.worked_solution:
First, from the equation of the plane we get that the normal vector of $Π$ is $n=⟨1,-1,4⟩.$

Now, we solve the Cartesian equation of $Π$ for $z$:

$$
\begin{aligned}x-y+4z+16 & =0 \\ z & =-\frac{1}{4}x+\frac{1}{4}y-4.\end{aligned}
$$

If we put, say, $x=0$ and $y=0$, we get $z=-4.$ Hence, the point $P(0,0,-4)$ lies on $Π.$ Note that the position vector of $P$ is $p=⟨0,0,-4⟩.$

Finally, we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}(r-p)\cdot n & =0 \\ (r-⟨0,0,-4⟩)\cdot ⟨1,-1,4⟩ & =0.\end{aligned}
$$

Question 12
?

Given the Cartesian equation 4x+4y−2z=0 of the plane Π, find an equation of Π in the form (r−p)⋅n=0.

a
(r−⟨0,0,−2⟩)⋅⟨−4,4,−2⟩=0
b
(r−⟨0,0,2⟩)⋅⟨4,4,2⟩=0
c
(r−⟨0,0,0⟩)⋅⟨4,−2,4⟩=0
d
(r−⟨0,0,0⟩)⋅⟨4,4,−2⟩=0
e
(r−⟨0,0,1⟩)⋅⟨2,4,−4⟩=0
Submit

decision.explanation: The coefficients give normal vector ⟨4,4,-2⟩, and the origin lies on the plane. Thus option d expands directly to 4x+4y-2z=0.

after.name: Question 12
after.problem: Given the Cartesian equation $4x+4y-2z=0$ of the plane $Π$, find an equation of $Π$ in the form $(r-p)\cdot n=0.$
after.worked_solution:
First, from the equation of the plane we get that the normal vector of $Π$ is $n=⟨4,4,-2⟩.$

Now, we solve the Cartesian equation of $Π$ for $z$:

$$
\begin{aligned}4x+4y-2z & =0 \\ 2z & =4x+4y \\ z & =2x+2y.\end{aligned}
$$

If we put, say, $x=0$ and $y=0$, we get $z=0.$ Hence, the point $P(0,0,0)$ lies on $Π.$ Note that the position vector of $P$ is $p=⟨0,0,0⟩.$

Finally, we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}(r-p)\cdot n & =0 \\ (r-⟨0,0,0⟩)\cdot ⟨4,4,-2⟩ & =0.\end{aligned}
$$

after.html:
Question 12
?

Given the Cartesian equation 4x+4y−2z=0 of the plane Π, find an equation of Π in the form (r−p)⋅n=0.

a
(r−⟨0,0,−2⟩)⋅⟨−4,4,−2⟩=0
b
(r−⟨0,0,2⟩)⋅⟨4,4,2⟩=0
c
(r−⟨0,0,0⟩)⋅⟨4,−2,4⟩=0
d
(r−⟨0,0,0⟩)⋅⟨4,4,−2⟩=0
e
(r−⟨0,0,1⟩)⋅⟨2,4,−4⟩=0
Submit
Correct
EXPLANATION

First, from the equation of the plane we get that the normal vector of Π is n=⟨4,4,−2⟩.

Now, we solve the Cartesian equation of Π for z: 4x+4y−2z=02z=4x+4yz=2x+2y. If we put, say, x=0 and y=0, we get z=0. Hence, the point P(0,0,0) lies on Π. Note that the position vector of P is p=⟨0,0,0⟩.

Finally, we obtain (r−p)⋅n=0(r−⟨0,0,0⟩)⋅⟨4,4,−2⟩=0.

content.knowledge_point: Finding the Vector Equation of a Plane Given Its Cartesian Equation
content.problem: Given the Cartesian equation $4x+4y-2z=0$ of the plane $Π$, find an equation of $Π$ in the form $(r-p)\cdot n=0.$
content.worked_solution:
First, from the equation of the plane we get that the normal vector of $Π$ is $n=⟨4,4,-2⟩.$

Now, we solve the Cartesian equation of $Π$ for $z$:

$$
\begin{aligned}4x+4y-2z & =0 \\ 2z & =4x+4y \\ z & =2x+2y.\end{aligned}
$$

If we put, say, $x=0$ and $y=0$, we get $z=0.$ Hence, the point $P(0,0,0)$ lies on $Π.$ Note that the position vector of $P$ is $p=⟨0,0,0⟩.$

Finally, we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}(r-p)\cdot n & =0 \\ (r-⟨0,0,0⟩)\cdot ⟨4,4,-2⟩ & =0.\end{aligned}
$$

Question 13
?

Given the Cartesian equation 2x+y−2z−4=0 of the plane Π, find an equation of Π in the form (r−p)⋅n=0.

a
(r−⟨0,0,2⟩)⋅⟨1,0,−1⟩=0
b
(r−⟨0,0,2⟩)⋅⟨2,1,−2⟩=0
c
(r−⟨0,0,−2⟩)⋅⟨2,1,−2⟩=0
d
(r−⟨0,0,−2⟩)⋅⟨2,0,−2⟩=0
e
(r−⟨0,0,−2⟩)⋅⟨2,−2,−4⟩=0
Submit

decision.explanation: The normal vector is ⟨2,1,-2⟩. Setting x=y=0 gives z=-2, so (0,0,-2) lies on the plane. Option c expands to 2x+y-2(z+2)=0, exactly the given equation.

after.name: Question 13
after.problem: Given the Cartesian equation $2x+y-2z-4=0$ of the plane $Π$, find an equation of $Π$ in the form $(r-p)\cdot n=0.$
after.worked_solution:
First, from the equation of the plane we get that the normal vector of $Π$ is $n=⟨2,1,-2⟩.$

Now, we solve the Cartesian equation of $Π$ for $z$:

$$
\begin{aligned}2x+y-2z-4 & =0 \\ -2z & =-2x-y+4 \\ z & =x+\frac{1}{2}y-2.\end{aligned}
$$

If we put, say, $x=0$ and $y=0$, we get $z=-2.$ Hence, the point $P(0,0,-2)$ lies on $Π.$ Note that the position vector of $P$ is $p=⟨0,0,-2⟩.$

Finally, we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}(r-p)\cdot n & =0 \\ (r-⟨0,0,-2⟩)\cdot ⟨2,1,-2⟩ & =0.\end{aligned}
$$

content.problem: Given the Cartesian equation $2x+y-2z-4=0$ of the plane $Π$, find an equation of $Π$ in the form $(r-p)\cdot n=0.$
content.worked_solution:
First, from the equation of the plane we get that the normal vector of $Π$ is $n=⟨2,1,-2⟩.$

Now, we solve the Cartesian equation of $Π$ for $z$:

$$
\begin{aligned}2x+y-2z-4 & =0 \\ -2z & =-2x-y+4 \\ z & =x+\frac{1}{2}y-2.\end{aligned}
$$

If we put, say, $x=0$ and $y=0$, we get $z=-2.$ Hence, the point $P(0,0,-2)$ lies on $Π.$ Note that the position vector of $P$ is $p=⟨0,0,-2⟩.$

Finally, we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}(r-p)\cdot n & =0 \\ (r-⟨0,0,-2⟩)\cdot ⟨2,1,-2⟩ & =0.\end{aligned}
$$

after.name: Question 16
after.problem: Find a Cartesian equation of the plane that passes through the points $A(1,-1,1)$, $P(2,0,3)$ and $Q(1,1,0).$
after.worked_solution:
Note that the position vectors of the points $A,P$ and $Q$ are $a=⟨1,-1,1⟩,\,p=⟨2,0,3⟩,$ and $q=⟨1,1,0⟩.$

First, using the $3$ points we build $2$ vectors parallel to the plane:

$$
\begin{aligned}{v}_{1} & =\overset{\to }{AP} \\  & =⟨2,0,3⟩-⟨1,-1,1⟩ \\  & =⟨1,1,2⟩ \\ {v}_{2} & =\overset{\to }{AQ} \\  & =⟨1,1,0⟩-⟨1,-1,1⟩ \\  & =⟨0,2,-1⟩\end{aligned}
$$

 

Now, we need to find the normal vector of the plane. To do that, we use the cross product of ${v}_{1}$ and ${v}_{2}$ as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}n & ={v}_{1}\times {v}_{2} \\  & =[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 1 \\ 2\end{aligned}]\times [\begin{aligned}0 \\ 2 \\ -1\end{aligned}] \\  & =\left|\begin{aligned}i & j & k \\ 1 & 1 & 2 \\ 0 & 2 & -1\end{aligned}\right| \\  & =-5i+j+2k \\  & =⟨-5,1,2⟩\end{aligned}
$$

Then, using the dot product, we can find the equation of the plane:

$$
\begin{aligned}(r-p)\cdot n & =0 \\ r\cdot n & =p\cdot n \\ r\cdot ⟨-5,1,2⟩ & =⟨2,0,3⟩\cdot ⟨-5,1,2⟩ \\ r\cdot ⟨-5,1,2⟩ & =-4\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, to obtain the Cartesian equation of the plane, we substitute $r=⟨x,y,z⟩$ into the equation above and get

$$
\begin{aligned}⟨x,y,z⟩\cdot ⟨-5,1,2⟩ & =-4 \\ -5x+y+2z & =-4 \\ -5x+y+2z+4 & =0 \\ 5x-y-2z-4 & =0.\end{aligned}
$$

Question 16

Find a Cartesian equation of the plane that passes through the points A(1,−1,1), P(2,0,3) and Q(1,1,0).

a
5x−y−2z−4=0
b
x−y−4=0
c
2x+3z−4=0
d
5x−y−2z=0
e
x−y+z+4=0
Submit
Correct
EXPLANATION

Note that the position vectors of the points A,P and Q are a=⟨1,−1,1⟩,p=⟨2,0,3⟩, and q=⟨1,1,0⟩.

First, using the 3 points we build 2 vectors parallel to the plane: v1=AP→=⟨2,0,3⟩−⟨1,−1,1⟩=⟨1,1,2⟩v2=AQ→=⟨1,1,0⟩−⟨1,−1,1⟩=⟨0,2,−1⟩

Now, we need to find the normal vector of the plane. To do that, we use the cross product of v1 and v2 as follows:

n=v1×v2=[112]×[02−1]=ijk11202−1=−5i+j+2k=⟨−5,1,2⟩

Then, using the dot product, we can find the equation of the plane:

(r−p)⋅n=0r⋅n=p⋅nr⋅⟨−5,1,2⟩=⟨2,0,3⟩⋅⟨−5,1,2⟩r⋅⟨−5,1,2⟩=−4

Finally, to obtain the Cartesian equation of the plane, we substitute r=⟨x,y,z⟩ into the equation above and get

⟨x,y,z⟩⋅⟨−5,1,2⟩=−4−5x+y+2z=−4−5x+y+2z+4=05x−y−2z−4=0.

content.knowledge_point: Finding the Cartesian Equation of the Plane Parallel To Two Vectors
content.problem: Find a Cartesian equation of the plane that passes through the points $A(1,-1,1)$, $P(2,0,3)$ and $Q(1,1,0).$
content.worked_solution:
Note that the position vectors of the points $A,P$ and $Q$ are $a=⟨1,-1,1⟩,\,p=⟨2,0,3⟩,$ and $q=⟨1,1,0⟩.$

First, using the $3$ points we build $2$ vectors parallel to the plane:

$$
\begin{aligned}{v}_{1} & =\overset{\to }{AP} \\  & =⟨2,0,3⟩-⟨1,-1,1⟩ \\  & =⟨1,1,2⟩ \\ {v}_{2} & =\overset{\to }{AQ} \\  & =⟨1,1,0⟩-⟨1,-1,1⟩ \\  & =⟨0,2,-1⟩\end{aligned}
$$

 

Now, we need to find the normal vector of the plane. To do that, we use the cross product of ${v}_{1}$ and ${v}_{2}$ as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}n & ={v}_{1}\times {v}_{2} \\  & =[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 1 \\ 2\end{aligned}]\times [\begin{aligned}0 \\ 2 \\ -1\end{aligned}] \\  & =\left|\begin{aligned}i & j & k \\ 1 & 1 & 2 \\ 0 & 2 & -1\end{aligned}\right| \\  & =-5i+j+2k \\  & =⟨-5,1,2⟩\end{aligned}
$$

Then, using the dot product, we can find the equation of the plane:

$$
\begin{aligned}(r-p)\cdot n & =0 \\ r\cdot n & =p\cdot n \\ r\cdot ⟨-5,1,2⟩ & =⟨2,0,3⟩\cdot ⟨-5,1,2⟩ \\ r\cdot ⟨-5,1,2⟩ & =-4\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, to obtain the Cartesian equation of the plane, we substitute $r=⟨x,y,z⟩$ into the equation above and get

$$
\begin{aligned}⟨x,y,z⟩\cdot ⟨-5,1,2⟩ & =-4 \\ -5x+y+2z & =-4 \\ -5x+y+2z+4 & =0 \\ 5x-y-2z-4 & =0.\end{aligned}
$$

$$
\begin{aligned}n & ={v}_{1}\times {v}_{2} \\  & =[\begin{aligned}5 \\ 2 \\ 1\end{aligned}]\times [\begin{aligned}0 \\ 3 \\ 3\end{aligned}] \\  & =\left|\begin{aligned}i & j & k \\ 5 & 2 & 1 \\ 0 & 3 & 3\end{aligned}\right| \\  & =3i-15j+15k \\  & =⟨3,-15,15⟩\end{aligned}

$$
\begin{aligned}(r-p)\cdot n & =0 \\ r\cdot n & =p\cdot n \\ r\cdot ⟨3,-15,15⟩ & =⟨1,0,3⟩\cdot ⟨3,-15,15⟩ \\ r\cdot ⟨3,-15,15⟩ & =48\end{aligned}

$$
\begin{aligned}{v}_{1} & =\overset{\to }{AP} \\  & =⟨5,0,3⟩-⟨2,-2,1⟩ \\  & =⟨3,2,2⟩ \\ {v}_{2} & =\overset{\to }{AQ} \\  & =⟨1,1,-1⟩-⟨2,-2,1⟩ \\  & =⟨-1,3,-2⟩\end{aligned}
$$

 

Now,  we need to find the normal vector of the plane. To do that, we use the cross product of ${v}_{1}$ and ${v}_{2}$ as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}n & ={v}_{1}\times {v}_{2} \\  & =[\begin{aligned}3 \\ 2 \\ 2\end{aligned}]\times [\begin{aligned}-1 \\ 3 \\ -2\end{aligned}] \\  & =\left|\begin{aligned}i & j & k \\ 3 & 2 & 2 \\ -1 & 3 & -2\end{aligned}\right| \\  & =-10i+4j+11k \\  & =⟨-10,4,11⟩\end{aligned}
$$

Then, using the dot product, we can find the equation of the plane:

$$
\begin{aligned}(r-p)\cdot n & =0 \\ r\cdot n & =p\cdot n \\ r\cdot ⟨-10,4,11⟩ & =⟨5,0,3⟩\cdot ⟨-10,4,11⟩ \\ r\cdot ⟨-10,4,11⟩ & =-17\end{aligned}

decision.explanation: AP=(2,1,1) and AQ=(-2,2,-2). Their cross product is (-4,2,6), so (4,-2,-6) is a normal. Its dot product with A is 4+4-18=-10, giving 4x-2y-6z+10=0, option e.

after.name: Question 19
after.problem: Find a Cartesian equation of the plane that passes through the points $A(1,-2,3)$, $P(3,-1,4)$ and $Q(-1,0,1).$
after.worked_solution:
Note that the position vectors of the points $A,P$ and $Q$ are $a=⟨1,-2,3⟩,\,p=⟨3,-1,4⟩,$ and $q=⟨-1,0,1⟩.$

First, using the $3$ points we build $2$ vectors parallel to the plane:

$$
\begin{aligned}{v}_{1} & =\overset{\to }{AP} \\  & =⟨3,-1,4⟩-⟨1,-2,3⟩ \\  & =⟨2,1,1⟩ \\ {v}_{2} & =\overset{\to }{AQ} \\  & =⟨-1,0,1⟩-⟨1,-2,3⟩ \\  & =⟨-2,2,-2⟩\end{aligned}
$$

 

Now,  we need to find the normal vector of the plane. To do that, we use the cross product of ${v}_{1}$ and ${v}_{2}$ as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}n & ={v}_{1}\times {v}_{2} \\  & =[\begin{aligned}2 \\ 1 \\ 1\end{aligned}]\times [\begin{aligned}-2 \\ 2 \\ -2\end{aligned}] \\  & =\left|\begin{aligned}i & j & k \\ 2 & 1 & 1 \\ -2 & 2 & -2\end{aligned}\right| \\  & =-4i+2j+6k \\  & =⟨-4,2,6⟩\end{aligned}
$$

Then, using the dot product, we can find the equation of the plane:

$$
\begin{aligned}(r-p)\cdot n & =0 \\ r\cdot n & =p\cdot n \\ r\cdot ⟨-4,2,6⟩ & =⟨3,-1,4⟩\cdot ⟨-4,2,6⟩ \\ r\cdot ⟨-4,2,6⟩ & =10\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, to obtain the Cartesian equation of the plane, we substitute $r=⟨x,y,z⟩$ into the equation above and get

$$
\begin{aligned}⟨x,y,z⟩\cdot ⟨-4,2,6⟩ & =10 \\ -4x+2y+6z & =10 \\ -4x+2y+6z-10 & =0 \\ 4x-2y-6z+10 & =0.\end{aligned}
$$

a
4x−2y+6z+21=0
b
4x−6y−2z+17=0

2x−4y−6z+13=0
d
4x−6y−2z+7=0

4x−2y−6z+10=0

EXPLANATION

Note that the position vectors of the points A,P and Q are a=⟨1,−2,3⟩,p=⟨3,−1,4⟩, and q=⟨−1,0,1⟩.

First, using the 3 points we build 2 vectors parallel to the plane:

v1=AP→=⟨3,−1,4⟩−⟨1,−2,3⟩=⟨2,1,1⟩v2=AQ→=⟨−1,0,1⟩−⟨1,−2,3⟩=⟨−2,2,−2⟩

Now, we need to find the normal vector of the plane. To do that, we use the cross product of v1 and v2 as follows:

n=v1×v2=[211]×[−22−2]=ijk211−22−2=−4i+2j+6k=⟨−4,2,6⟩

Then, using the dot product, we can find the equation of the plane:

(r−p)⋅n=0r⋅n=p⋅nr⋅⟨−4,2,6⟩=⟨3,−1,4⟩⋅⟨−4,2,6⟩r⋅⟨−4,2,6⟩=10

Finally, to obtain the Cartesian equation of the plane, we substitute r=⟨x,y,z⟩ into the equation above and get

⟨x,y,z⟩⋅⟨−4,2,6⟩=10−4x+2y+6z=10−4x+2y+6z−10=04x−2y−6z+10=0.

content.knowledge_point: Finding the Cartesian Equation of the Plane Parallel To Two Vectors
content.problem: Find a Cartesian equation of the plane that passes through the points $A(1,-2,3)$, $P(3,-1,4)$ and $Q(-1,0,1).$
content.worked_solution:
Note that the position vectors of the points $A,P$ and $Q$ are $a=⟨1,-2,3⟩,\,p=⟨3,-1,4⟩,$ and $q=⟨-1,0,1⟩.$

First, using the $3$ points we build $2$ vectors parallel to the plane:

$$
\begin{aligned}{v}_{1} & =\overset{\to }{AP} \\  & =⟨3,-1,4⟩-⟨1,-2,3⟩ \\  & =⟨2,1,1⟩ \\ {v}_{2} & =\overset{\to }{AQ} \\  & =⟨-1,0,1⟩-⟨1,-2,3⟩ \\  & =⟨-2,2,-2⟩\end{aligned}
$$

 

Now,  we need to find the normal vector of the plane. To do that, we use the cross product of ${v}_{1}$ and ${v}_{2}$ as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}n & ={v}_{1}\times {v}_{2} \\  & =[\begin{aligned}2 \\ 1 \\ 1\end{aligned}]\times [\begin{aligned}-2 \\ 2 \\ -2\end{aligned}] \\  & =\left|\begin{aligned}i & j & k \\ 2 & 1 & 1 \\ -2 & 2 & -2\end{aligned}\right| \\  & =-4i+2j+6k \\  & =⟨-4,2,6⟩\end{aligned}
$$

Then, using the dot product, we can find the equation of the plane:

$$
\begin{aligned}(r-p)\cdot n & =0 \\ r\cdot n & =p\cdot n \\ r\cdot ⟨-4,2,6⟩ & =⟨3,-1,4⟩\cdot ⟨-4,2,6⟩ \\ r\cdot ⟨-4,2,6⟩ & =10\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, to obtain the Cartesian equation of the plane, we substitute $r=⟨x,y,z⟩$ into the equation above and get

$$
\begin{aligned}⟨x,y,z⟩\cdot ⟨-4,2,6⟩ & =10 \\ -4x+2y+6z & =10 \\ -4x+2y+6z-10 & =0 \\ 4x-2y-6z+10 & =0.\end{aligned}
$$
